ae36de8e80.q: How does Linde use AI to improve driver efficiency in its fleet of 1 billion kilometers driven annually?
ae36de8e80.a: Linde developed a driver training tool powered by a sophisticated AI algorithm that analyzes big data from onboard computers to understand parameters like harsh braking, acceleration, delivery frequency, and terrain type. The system correlates drivers' driving behavior with fuel consumption, enabling fair and accurate predictions of how each driver's style influences fuel efficiency. Drivers receive feedback after each trip via an app with gamification elements, allowing them to improve systematically without complex statistics.

6b92363605.q: What is the biggest question to ask before starting an AI project in supply chain?
6b92363605.a: The most critical question is why you want to implement AI—understanding the business objective, desired outcomes, and end users who will act on the software. Design thinking methodology helps clarify what value you want to add and who will use the solution. Only after this clarity should you search for data scientists or partners, as the business case and domain expertise matter far more than the algorithms themselves.

2b93c3598e.q: How can AI improve demand forecasting accuracy by incorporating external events like Oktoberfest?
2b93c3598e.a: AI enables demand forecasting that incorporates both internal historical sales data and external real-time data including events, weather, and population behavior. For example, Linde uses Oktoberfest—a major event in Munich—as a signal in its CO2 demand forecasting algorithm because the event significantly influences customer demand from restaurants and bars. The algorithm learns these dynamic patterns to achieve much higher forecasting accuracy than traditional methods.

e431772b76.q: What role does feature engineering and domain expertise play in building AI segmentation models?
e431772b76.a: Feature engineering—identifying which business characteristics matter—is the most important part of AI model building and requires domain expertise from your company, not data scientists. For customer segmentation, relevant features might include SKU size, delivery frequency, or customer buying behavior. Once features are defined, standard clustering algorithms like K-means or K-prototype can be applied, followed by iterative interpretation to understand what the segments mean for your business.
